arxiv-1707-02562.title: Determination of the strong coupling constant α s \alpha_{\mathrm{s}} from transverse energy–energy correlations in multijet events at s = 8 ​ TeV \sqrt{s}=8\penalty\ \text{Te\kern-1.00006ptV} using the ATLAS detector
arxiv-1707-02562.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1707-02562.description: Abstract Measurements of transverse energy–energy correlations and their associated asymmetries in multi-jet events using the ATLAS detector at the LHC are presented. The data used correspond to s = 8 ​ TeV \sqrt{s}=8\penalty\ \text{Te\kern-1.00006ptV} proton–proton collisions with an integrated luminosity of 20.2 fb -1 .

arxiv-2102-00751.title: Learning to Combat Noisy Labels via Classification Margins
arxiv-2102-00751.creator: Jason Z. Lin, Jelena Bradic
arxiv-2102-00751.description: Abstract A deep neural network trained on noisy labels is known to quickly lose its power to discriminate clean instances from noisy ones. After the early learning phase has ended, the network memorizes the noisy instances, which leads to a significant degradation in its generalization performance.

arxiv-2103-06451.title: Automorphisms of free braided associative algebras in two variables
arxiv-2103-06451.description: Abstract . We describe the groups of automorphisms of two generated free braided associative algebras with involutive diagonal braidings over a field of characteristic ≠ 2 \neq 2 . Depending on the form of the diagonal involutive braiding, five different automorphism groups arise as automorphism groups of two generated free braided associative algebras.

arxiv-2107-01304.title: Qubit-based clock synchronization for QKD systems using a Bayesian approach
arxiv-2107-01304.creator: Roderick D. Cochran, Daniel J. Gauthier
arxiv-2107-01304.description: Abstract Quantum key distribution (QKD) systems provide a method for two users to exchange a provably secure key. Synchronizing the users’ clocks is an essential step before a secure key can be distilled. Qubit-based synchronization protocols directly use the transmitted quantum states to achieve synchronization and thus avoid the need for additional classical synchronization hardware.

arxiv-2109-11185.title: Investigation of the subsurface structure of a sunspot based on the spatial distribution of oscillation centers inferred from umbral flashes
arxiv-2109-11185.creator: Kyuhyoun Cho, Jongchul Chae, Maria S. Madjarska
arxiv-2109-11185.description: Abstract The subsurface structure of a solar sunspot is important in the stability of the sunspots and the energy transport therein. Two subsurface structure models have been proposed, the monolithic and cluster models, but no clear observational evidence supporting a particular model has been found so far.

arxiv-2311-13771.title: Work-Efficient Parallel Derandomization II: Optimal Concentrations via Bootstrapping
arxiv-2311-13771.creator: Mohsen Ghaffari, Christoph Grunau
arxiv-2311-13771.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mohsen Ghaffari, Christoph Grunau. In this paper, we present an efficient parallel derandomization method for randomized algorithms that rely on concentrations such as the Chernoff bound. This settles a classic problem in parallel derandomization, which dates back to the 1980s.

arxiv-2402-10751.creator: Aven-Le ZHOU, Lei XI, Kang Zhang
arxiv-2402-10751.description: Abstract . In Flusserian view of media history, humans often misperceive the world projected by media to be the world itself, leading to a loss of freedom. This paper examines Flusserian Freedom in the context of Mixed Reality (MR) and explores how humans can recognize the obscuration of the world within the media (i.e., MR) and understand their relationship.

arxiv-2402-11363.description: Abstract Tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) stands as the predominant high-throughput technique for comprehensively analyzing protein content within biological samples. This methodology is a cornerstone driving the advancement of proteomics. In recent years, substantial strides have been made in Data-Independent Acquisition (DIA) strategies, facilitating impartial and non-targeted fragmentation of precursor ions.

arxiv-2410-19766.title: Large Model for Small Data: Foundation Model for Cross-Modal RF Human Activity Recognition
arxiv-2410-19766.creator: Yuxuan Weng 1 , Guoquan Wu 1 , Tianyue Zheng 1,2 🖂 , Yanbing Yang 3 , Jun Luo 4
arxiv-2410-19766.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yuxuan Weng 1 , Guoquan Wu 1 , Tianyue Zheng 1,2 🖂 , Yanbing Yang 3 , Jun Luo 4. Radio-Frequency (RF)-based Human Activity Recognition (HAR) rises as a promising solution for applications unamenable to techniques requiring computer visions. However, the scarcity of labeled RF data due to their non-interpretable nature poses a significant obstacle.

arxiv-2503-22141.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence with Human Expertise: An In-depth Analysis of ChatGPT’s Capabilities in Generating Metamorphic Relations
arxiv-2503-22141.creator: Yifan Zhang, Dave Towey*, Matthew Pike, Quang-Hung Luu, Huai Liu, and Tsong Yueh Chen
arxiv-2503-22141.description: Abstract Context: This paper provides an in-depth examination of the generation and evaluation of Metamorphic Relations (MRs) using GPT models developed by OpenAI, with a particular focus on the capabilities of GPT-4 in software testing environments. Objective: The aim is to examine the quality of MRs produced by GPT-3.

arxiv-2508-02276.title: CellForge: Agentic Design of Virtual Cell Models
arxiv-2508-02276.creator: Xiangru Tang, Zhuoyun Yu, Jiapeng Chen, Yan Cui, Daniel Shao, Weixu Wang H
arxiv-2508-02276.description: Abstract Virtual cell modeling represents an emerging frontier at the intersection of artificial intelligence and biology, aiming to predict quantities such as responses to diverse perturbations quantitatively. However, autonomously building computational models for virtual cells is challenging due to the complexity of biological systems, the heterogeneity of data modalities, and the need for domain-specific expertise across multiple disciplines.

arxiv-2510-06662.title: The Effect of Attention Head Count on Transformer Approximation
arxiv-2510-06662.creator: Penghao Yu, Zeyu Bao, Haotian Jiang, Ruoxi Yu, Qianxiao Li
arxiv-2510-06662.description: Abstract Transformer has become the dominant architecture for sequence modeling, yet a detailed understanding of how its structural parameters influence expressive power remains limited. In this work, we study the approximation properties of transformers, with particular emphasis on the role of the number of attention heads.

pmc-10499790.title: Disrupting iron homeostasis can potentiate colistin activity and overcome colistin resistance mechanisms in Gram-Negative Bacteria
pmc-10499790.creator: Kavita Gadar, Rubén de Dios, Nikol Kadeřábková, Thomas A K Prescott, Despoina A I Mavridou, Ronan R McCarthy
pmc-10499790.description: Acinetobacter baumannii is a Gram-negative priority pathogen that can readily overcome antibiotic treatment through a range of intrinsic and acquired resistance mechanisms. Treatment of carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii largely relies on the use of colistin in cases where other treatment options have been exhausted. However, the emergence of resistance against this last-line drug has significantly increased amongst clinical strains.

pmc-11531299.creator: Ping Wu, Xin Qian, Yijing Hu, Xiaoxia Yan
pmc-11531299.description: ObjectiveThe objective of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to assess the effectiveness of TIMT on pulmonary function in children and adolescents with asthma.MethodWe searched for randomized controlled clinical trials in the MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CINAHL, Sino Med, Wan fang, CNKI, and VIP until March 2024.

pmc-11674301.title: Flexible Electrochemical Biosensor Using Nanostructure-Modified Polymer Electrode for Detection of Viral Nucleic Acids
pmc-11674301.creator: Jiyu Han, Yejin Lee, Jin-Ho Lee, Jinho Yoon
pmc-11674301.description: In the biosensor field, the accurate detection of contagious disease has become one of the most important research topics in the post-pandemic period. However, conventional contagious viral biosensors normally require chemical modifications to introduce the probe molecules to nucleic acids such as a redox indicator, fluorescent dye, or quencher for biosensing.

pmc-12639288.title: A data-driven approach to optimizing waiting times in outpatient pharmacy services: Interrupted time series analysis
pmc-12639288.creator: Hazzaa Alghamdi, Talal S. Alshihayb, Yazeed Alharbi, Mohammad Alawagi, Abdullah Aleissa, Yasser Albogami
pmc-12639288.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundOperational efficiency in outpatient pharmacies is a critical factor in healthcare delivery, directly impacting patient satisfaction and adherence to prescribed treatments. pmc-13025480.title: N-Acetylcysteine Reduces Tissue Injury Induced by Oxygen–Glucose Deprivation in an Organotypic Culture of Mouse Cerebral Cortex Slices
pmc-13025480.creator: Claudia Villani, Angelo Di Clemente, Roberto William Invernizzi, Rossano Rezzonico
pmc-13025480.description: Highlights What are the main findings? •In an in vitro model of hypoxic–ischemic cell death, N-acetylcysteine exerts a direct, concentration-dependent cytoprotective effect on cerebral cortex slices whether administered before or after oxygen–glucose deprivation.•N-acetylcysteine is more potent in reducing cellular damage in cerebral cortex slices derived from female mice than in those from male mice.

pmc-13166811.title: Segmental femoral fracture management using intramedullary nailing combined with plate fixation: a case report
pmc-13166811.creator: Muhammad Ade Junaidi, Wahyu Eko Jatmiko
pmc-13166811.description: Introduction:Segmental femoral fractures are challenging, with a high risk of non-union, requiring tailored treatments such as intramedullary nailing (IMN) and plate fixation. Although this combined approach is promising for tibial fractures, its effectiveness in segmental femoral fractures remains under evaluation. This study aims to evaluate the success rates of IMN and plate fixation in treating these challenging injuries.

pmc-13349366.title: NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation in Oxidative Stress: A Key Mechanism Driving Neuroinflammation
pmc-13349366.creator: Crisalde Ramirez-Celis, Ari Misael Martínez-Torres, Julio Morán
pmc-13349366.description: BackgroundIn acquired and neurodegenerative brain diseases, inflammation-mediated neuronal death contributes to the deterioration of neurological deficits in patients. In the innate immune system, the NLRP3 inflammasome is a cytosolic complex that regulates the release of proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18, thereby amplifying the inflammatory response and neuronal damage.

pmc-13356902.title: AbTune: layer-wise selective fine-tuning of protein language models for antibodies
pmc-13356902.creator: Xiaotong Xu, Alexandre M J J Bonvin
pmc-13356902.description: Antibodies play central roles in immune defense and are widely used as therapeutic agents. However, the high structural and sequence diversity of antigen-binding loops, combined with limited experimental data and weak co-evolutionary signals, makes it difficult to develop generalizable predictive models.

pmc-13445183.title: Domain-specific trends in healthy life expectancy among Chinese older adults: Compression, expansion, and dynamic equilibrium
pmc-13445183.creator: Kaishan Jiao, Yujin Song, Wen Hu
pmc-13445183.description: BackgroundAmid rising global life expectancy, the debate over whether population aging entails a “compression” or an “expansion” of morbidity remains unresolved. Previous evidence, drawn largely from Western nations and often reliant on cross-sectional data or single health indicators, has produced mixed findings.
